title: Aza'raan Language Source-only Continuation (24 chapters)

sections.title: Two Foundations, Many Voices
sections.text:
The Kaʻaheʻanua people brought a Fenua language shaped for the project by Proto-Oceanic structures.
Uxrowoiye speakers already had their own speech and hieroglyph-derived written tradition.
The first Aza’raan was not either language alone.
It emerged where survivors needed to speak with one another while preserving names, ceremonies, and records.
Later immigration added new sounds, borrowed words, translations, and prestige registers.
Treat this history as a sequence of human and nonhuman communities making choices, not an instant equal blending of every language.
Historical and system reference
The source MMORPG describes Aza'raans as descendants of Kaʻaheʻanua sorcerers and Uxrowoiye psychics. A shared language emerges from contact between these specific communities, not from the instant disappearance of either parent language. Preserve the distinction between linguistic ancestry and genetic ancestry. Historical mixed communities, including Kalus’aans, Kalusogals, and Aza’ziras, provide plausible bilingual transmission routes, but their native grammars are not yet independently documented.
Next chapter

sections.title: Before the Cataclysm
sections.text:
Uxrowo had a native psionic civilization with its own language and pictographic records.
Fenua’s Kaʻaheʻanua community existed independently.
Uxrowoiye records used reassigned Egyptian-inspired figures as meaningful written signs; they did not use the alphabet of modern Earth.
The two lineages must remain legible in place names, ritual words, and inherited sign meanings even after the shared language emerges.
Next chapter

sections.title: 1351 BCE Convergence
sections.text:
The Cataclysm transformed Uxrowo and created the conditions under which the newcomers and Uxrowoiye could no longer live separately.
Emergency coordination favored quickly learnable particles and shared everyday terms.
Formal writing retained the weight of older Uxrowoiye symbols.
This is the start of the linguistic convergence, not proof that all languages became identical in a single generation.
The 1351 BCE planetary event is distinguished from the later destruction of the continent Belavadös by the Iron Dominion.
Historical and system reference
The old Uxrowoiye document presents the early period as a coexisting dual system with competing spoken and written conventions. This supports gradual convergence: learners can borrow a grammatical particle from one lineage while continuing to use a different lineage's family terminology or record-keeping marks. The earlier 132-sign count in that document is superseded by the author's current 52-letter rule.
Next chapter

sections.title: Proto Aza’raan, 52 Letters
sections.text:
The working Proto-Aza’raan inventory has exactly 52 letter values, including early distinctions subsequently lost or merged.
The source Letter Evolution Table preserves 52 ancestral glyph rows.
Use them as provenance for letter-design studies, not as finished modern letterforms.
The count excludes convenient duplicates of a character caused by word position or artistic calligraphy.
The glottal stop and click belonged to the ancient sound system.
Their later representation needs a recorded change history.
Historical and system reference
Next chapter

sections.title: Uxrowoiye Hieroglyph Origins
sections.text:
Every new glyph proposal must cite an identified source sign, its Uxrowoiye meaning, its proposed phonetic reassignment, and the alterations visible in each era.
The letter should be traceable from recognizable picture, to shorthand, to a standardized pen stroke, to modern independent and subscript forms.
A sign that cannot be traced should stay a design proposal.
The legacy glyph assignments remain useful even where the old alphabet counts are obsolete.
Historical and system reference
The uploaded English-alphabet study documents a useful real-world process: pictures can be reused as phonetic signs, sounds may be reassigned, and writing can change without every symbol having a single direct descendant. Use that method to design Aza'raan, while preserving the fictional Uxrowoiye meanings assigned to Egyptian-looking signs. Do not import Phoenician, Greek, or Latin as an in-world intermediate stage.
Next chapter

sections.title: Kaʻaheʻanua Sound Inheritance
sections.text:
Kaʻaheʻanua contributes an open, vowel-friendly syllable flow and social vocabulary to the merged language.
Existing Fenua names deserve stable pronunciation and capitalization rather than forced conversion into Uxrowoiye-looking spellings.
Proto-Oceanic is a real comparative inspiration, not evidence of a literal undocumented migration of an Earth-language family into fiction.
Verify examples against the original Kaʻaheʻanua reference rather than inventing unmarked translations.
Historical and system reference
The Kaʻaheʻanua language source records open syllables, vowel prominence and glottalization. These can inform the founding contact layer, but its older claim of exclusive Proto-Polynesian derivation conflicts with the latest Proto-Oceanic guidance. Proto-Oceanic remains the principal real-world inspiration; older formulations are research history only.
Next chapter

sections.title: Other Peoples as Language Makers
sections.text:
Kaluseban, Tamhiogal, Dril’thar, Deorbasun, Gandirosha, Gwynis, Geisamahi, Panolima, Volsarii, Azrahai, Jaspey, and Aburata peoples participate in centuries of exchange.
Contact can leave kinship terminology, practical trade vocabulary, ritual formulas, accents and loan names.
These are independently named communities; shared ancestry does not erase their speech differences.
The exact native grammar of each people remains an open research task where the original source documents do not specify it.
Historical and system reference
A language-contact record should distinguish trade words, inherited kinship terms, prestige borrowings, ritual conservatism, bilingual code-switching, phonological accommodation and script adoption. Include each contributing people by canonical name and mark candidate records. Ampharils are Dril'thar ancestry, not a second independent contact source.
Next chapter

sections.title: Dril’thar Inheritance
sections.text:
The Dril’thars are an amphibious people whose old MMORPG account connects them with water spirits and shore environments.
Their six strict-JSON environmental variants provide room for distinct reef, marsh, forest, ocean, rainforest and grassland regional speech.
Ampharils have already been merged into this people.
An old Ampharil entry can be retained as historical ancestry or an older dialect label, but never treated as an independent modern species or counted as another language-contact community.
Historical and system reference
The current species JSON recognizes six Dril'thar environmental variants. Record local regional terms under the Dril'thar branch rather than fabricating six separate species or imposing a single coastal pronunciation everywhere. Dril'thar signs for water, marsh, current and rainfall need source attestations before entering the approved dictionary.
Next chapter

sections.title: Kaluseban and Mixed Lineages
sections.text:
Kaluseban has six named strict-JSON bloodline variants.
The old MMORPG also records Kalus’aans, mixed Aza’raan and Kaluseban heritage, and Kalusogals, mixed aquatic Tamhiogal and oceanic Kaluseban heritage.
These names support multilingual households and local naming conventions without implying that mixed families belong to isolated biological species.
A mixed community can foster code-switching and new particles while remaining part of existing people.
Historical and system reference
The archived race list names Kalus’aans and Kalusogals among mixed-ancestry communities. These are valuable contact-setting evidence because multilingual households can move particles and honorifics between communities. They are not automatically newly approved species or evidence of a uniform Kaluseban accent.
Next chapter

sections.title: Ocean, Wetland and Coastal Speech
sections.text:
Tamhiogal and Dril’thar traditions encounter Kaluseban oceanic communities at ports and through travel.
Terms for tide, depth, reef, vessel, seasonal migration and navigational warnings are plausible borrowing domains.
Their exact sounds and word roots should only be finalized after consulting source language sheets.
A port-born Aza’raan register may preserve archaic names that are unusual in inland Modern Aza’raan.
Next chapter

sections.title: Other Regional Voices
sections.text:
The old MMORPG separately names Zirramunis, Garuraqets and Iamhaziras.
They should not vanish because the newer strict JSON has not yet assigned them a canonical entry.
Keep their source descriptions in a reconciliation register and distinguish them from author-approved species.
Their potential linguistic influence is a documented question, not a license to invent ancestral vocabulary.
New words generated from their influence are draft forms.
Historical and system reference
The source-backed names Zirramunis, Garuraqets and Iamhaziras warrant entries in the historical race concordance. Their spellings alone do not justify inventing complete phoneme inventories. Archive-only names such as Auridens or Sidherins stay below the approval threshold and have no automatic generator profile.
Next chapter

sections.title: Classical Aza’raan
sections.text:
Classical Aza’raan, especially relevant to campaigns on Belavadös, is approximately 80 percent particle-oriented.
Subjects and objects may move for emphasis when particles preserve their roles.
Chronicles, legal testimony, domestic conversation and poetry can employ different registers.
A historical word may retain a final consonant that later spelling would treat as exceptional.
The classical script belongs to a distinct phase between the 52-letter ancient register and later Modern 38-letter usage.
Historical and system reference
For the classical period, preserve flexible word order and roughly 80 percent particle-reliant grammar. Examples must indicate agent, patient, tense, certainty and emphasis without presuming Latin noun cases. A particle table should distinguish fixed meanings from proposed tests, and should not present a generated draft word as a translation.
Next chapter

sections.title: Intermediate Sound Changes
sections.text:
Vowels can merge when adults from different communities use the same term; clusters can split in careful ceremonial speech and collapse in everyday markets.
Every proposed sound change requires a before form, after form, estimated era, affected community, and plausible mechanism.
Avoid universal changes that supposedly reach every settlement overnight.
Existing archival notes document candidate processes, but conflicting old counts and anachronistic descriptions do not override the newest project rules.
Next chapter

sections.title: Transitional Aza’raan
sections.text:
The post-Cataclysm world, expanded road networks and later industrial settlements create conditions for more shared speech, not linguistic uniformity.
Transitional Aza’raan should preserve older verbal particles and regional loans.
In the MMORPG, characters may encounter archaic writing without needing the destroyed continent of Belavadös to exist as a playable land.
Historical sources can appear as objects, archives and inherited songs.
Historical and system reference
The transitional stage must preserve continuity between the older Uxrowoiye pictorial root shapes and independent or subscript forms seen in modern writing. This is a stage of change, not an unexplained replacement alphabet. Record what a scribe would simplify when using a brush, reed, carving tool, or later printer.
Next chapter

sections.title: Modern Aza’raan, 38 Letters
sections.text:
The authoritative modern target is a 38-letter system.
It includes compound sound letters and sound families rather than assuming 38 English-style keys.
One base sign may cover modern w, v and b in defined contexts.
Separate consonant-vowel letters can represent wah, weh and wee.
The W’i of W’iosamn and the mn sound in the same name each require one written character.
Their Latin spellings do not define glyph counts.
Historical and system reference
Next chapter

sections.title: Independent and Subscript Forms
sections.text:
A full independent letter occupies a normal writing unit.
A subscript derivative fits under, beside, or into an anchor where allowed by the spelling rules.
Khmer writing is an inspiration for the system of dependent positioning, but its actual letters are not transplanted.
For each of the 38 target graphemes, a chart should show independent shape, subscript shape, permitted combination, and one historical ancestor.
A positional allograph must not be accidentally counted as an extra letter.
Historical and system reference
A glyph design record needs anchor shape, independent form, subscript attachment point, stroke count, joining rule, collision avoidance and reading order. Draw each proposed sign at manuscript scale and small-screen scale. Subscript forms are visual alternates, not extra alphabet slots.
Next chapter

sections.title: Pronunciation and Phoneme Audit
sections.text:
Modern Aza’raan preserves a rolled or tapped r with ceremonial registers favoring a full trill.
Tz has the compound Taz value.
W’i functions as wee.
Mn is a single compound consonant unit associated with mhn.
The retained source table contains additional affricates, vowels, nasal sounds and glottal values.
Where their modern assignments conflict with the 38-letter rule, leave the mapping open pending deliberate author approval.
Next chapter

sections.title: Particles and Flexible Order
sections.text:
The modern language is approximately 90 percent particle-based.
Topic, agent, patient, tense, aspect, evidential, negation, direction, and relationship particles can carry roles that English expresses through word position or inflection.
Give each example a particle-by-particle gloss; no invented Aza’raan sentence should masquerade as a certified translation.
Flexible word order must never mean that a changed sentence becomes uninterpretable.
Historical and system reference
Particles should carry grammatical roles, temporal relationships, evidence, emphasis and social orientation in independently tested categories. The original word generator lists approximately fifty semantic particle categories, which can seed a lexicon design queue without constituting final spoken Aza'raan.
Next chapter

sections.title: Pronouns and Identity
sections.text:
Pronouns derive from cultural identity terms rather than assuming the English he/she distinction.
Source-era inventories contain different counts; the current guide can state the principle without silently settling conflicting inventories.
Record self-identified name, pronoun, speech register, relationship and appropriate context.
A language-contact model should also recognize that kinship and identity terms are often borrowed among neighboring peoples.
Historical and system reference
The older language documents mention 15 identity categories and an identity-derived pronoun system. Preserve any attested pronouns, but check them against the newer naming guide before determining whether a form is regional, historical or modern. Do not infer gender from appearance or species.
Next chapter

sections.title: Names and Inherited Spellings
sections.text:
W’iosamn, Arzuhan, Dakaroth, Belavadös and Tzaphaer keep historical romanizations unless a source-approved modern spelling replaces them.
Most everyday modern words tend toward vowel endings, while proper nouns and archival words may keep consonant endings.
Mixing ancestry may influence name sounds, but a character name should not be randomly reshaped to fit a temporary generator setting.
Next chapter

sections.title: Dictionary Provenance
sections.text:
Each dictionary entry records its meaning, era, community, original source, confidence, phonemic segments, written form and optional glyph lineage.
Separate approved vocabulary from newly generated candidates.
When two communities have the same gloss, preserve both forms until a documented borrowing or merger is established.
Dictionary export should be editable JSON so author-approved forms can remain stable.
Historical and system reference
An approved dictionary entry requires a meaning, era, sound rendering, grammatical role, source attestation, community or region, script form and review status. Generator output begins at draft status. Its listed contacts indicate design ingredients, not proven etymologies.
Next chapter

sections.title: Translation Method
sections.text:
Translation must specify which Aza’raan era and register is wanted.
Break the English source into propositions, choose semantic roles, select evidenced words, then add grammatical particles and attested ordering.
Mark unattested terms as missing, not as automatically invented equivalents.
Back-translate proposed sentences and report where meaning drift occurs.
Keep pronouns and names as author controlled choices.
Next chapter

sections.title: Word Generator Rules
sections.text:
The generator is a proposal tool with selectable contact communities and meanings, not a machine that declares new canon.
It should show chosen era, syllable count, allowed consonants and vowels, origin streams and a draft tag.
Exports should preserve the chosen sources and permit review.
Only explicitly approved forms enter the authoritative dictionary.
Ampharil is an alias for Dril’thar heritage and must never yield two separate influences.
Historical and system reference
The provided HTML generator has independent, anchor and subscript letter groups alongside noun and particle taxonomies. A new generator must preserve those categories or document why a particular archaic character cannot be mapped to the modern 38. The companion script workbench now records proposed derivations directly against each of the 52 assigned source roots.
Next chapter

sections.title: Writing System Review
sections.text:
For every sign, trace the assigned hieroglyph to proto outline, intermediate stroke economy, classical form and modern form.
The English alphabet document illustrates the general process of pictograms becoming phonetic signs and adapting through cultures.
It does not provide literal Aza’raan ancestry.
Do not replace the 52 Uxrowoiye sign references with Latin letters.
Produce black-and-white form studies and leave unverified shapes visibly labeled proposed.
Historical and system reference
Quality checks include reading order, strokes that remain visible at 16 pixels, identification under reduced vision, and distinct forms for lookalike roots. Any glyph chart lacking an attested source assignment should be labeled an illustration rather than a linguistic fact.

Appendix B: Hieroglyph root studies
The plates are experimental changes of stroke geometry. They are not final glyph assignments for the Modern 38.
Research: Lexical Evidence Across Four Eras
07 | Other Peoples as Language Makers
Research workflow: record each proposed loanword with the source community, time period, regional context, original written form, probable sound accommodation and evidence level. A Dril'thar environmental register can contain distinct regional terms without treating Ampharils as an independent people. Source file citations are mandatory before an entry can be called attested.
08 | Dril’thar Inheritance
Dril'thar inherited amphibious heritage includes the merged Ampharil material. Contact registers must not double count that ancestry. Distinguish six source-described Dril'thar environmental variants from six independent languages. The older root spelling of a place can coexist with a modern pronunciation only when both are cited.
16 | Independent and Subscript Forms
Dictionary workflow: the Word Forge generates unapproved drafts. The new lexicon evidence register can store Proto, Classical, Transitional and Modern spellings, plus source passages and community contact. A proposed borrowing is not the same as an attested native word; neither is author-approved automatically.
19 | Pronouns and Identity
Historical scripts should preserve one verified path from an original Uxrowoiye full-word sign through reduced strokes and sound use before proposing dependent or independent modern forms. The alphabet-history reference is an analogy for historical change, not a literal source alphabet for Aza'ra.
Evidence standard
A source-attested item requires a document and passage. A proposed borrowing must name the community and indicate that its sound and grammar are unverified. Authored approval must be a separate action from saving a draft.

warning: These supporting sources are not the authoritative new 19-letter language model or newer book manuscript. Repeated and old version titles are historical, not an instruction to rename anything.
